verses.1:
For the choirmaster. According to Gittith. + 84:1 Gittith is probably a musical or liturgical term; here and in Psalms 8 and 81. A Psalm of the sons of Korah.
 How lovely is Your dwelling place,
 O LORD of Hosts!
verses.2:
My soul longs, even faints,
 for the courts of the LORD;
 my heart and my flesh cry out
 for the living God.
verses.3:
Even the sparrow has found a home,
 and the swallow a nest for herself,
 where she places her young near Your altars,
 O LORD of Hosts, my King and my God.
verses.4:
How blessed are those who dwell in Your house!
 They are ever praising You.
 Selah
verses.5:
Blessed are those whose strength is in You,
 whose hearts are set on pilgrimage.
verses.7:
They go from strength to strength,
 until each appears before God in Zion.
verses.9:
Take notice of our shield, O God,
 and look with favor on the face of Your anointed.
verses.10:
For better is one day in Your courts
 than a thousand elsewhere.
 I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God
 than dwell in the tents of the wicked.
verses.12:
O LORD of Hosts,
 how blessed is the man who trusts in You!

metadata.source: Derived from the Berean Standard Bible (BSB). Missing verses restored from the Textus Receptus tradition for completeness.
